name: int8_polyeval
targeted_gap: reg_bytes_per_elem counts only memory-op slabs, not live fp32 temporaries; tiny int8 storage width green-lights a wide tile whose real fp32 working set spills at num_warps=4
hypothesis: int8 storage (itemsize 1) => bpe=4 (3 loads+1 store) => budget_target=8192//4=2048; reg_bpe=16 (4 ops*fp32) => reg_cap=4096, so budget wins => seed [1,2048]. But the body holds ~10 live fp32 tiles (3 inputs + p0..p6) = ~80KB/program resident, ~2.5x the 32KB the reg model counts, with the default 4 warps => register spill vs the default [32,32] tile which is small enough to stay resident. Expect seed >10% slower.
code:
@helion.kernel()
def int8_polyeval(a, b, c):
    out = torch.empty_like(a)
    for tm, tn in hl.tile(a.size()):
        x = a[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        y = b[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        z = c[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        p0 = x * x * x + y * y - z
        p1 = (x + y) * (y + z) * (z + x)
        p2 = x * y * z + p0 - p1
        p3 = (p0 * p1 - p2) * (x - y + z)
        p4 = p3 * p2 + p1 * p0 - x * y
        p5 = (p4 - p3 + p2 - p1 + p0) * (x + 1.0)
        p6 = p5 * p4 - p3 * p2 + p1 * p0
        r = (p0 + p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5 + p6) * 0.015625
        out[tm, tn] = r.to(out.dtype)
    return out

def make_inputs(shape):
    M, N = shape
    g = lambda: torch.randint(-4, 4, (M, N), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int8)
    return (g(), g(), g())

name: int8_bitwise_heavy
targeted_gap: 4 int8 inputs (itemsize 1) keep bytes_per_elem small so the byte model sizes a wide tile, but the many live fp32 intermediates the reg model never counts overflow the register file at num_warps=4
hypothesis: bpe=5 (4 loads+1 store, int8) => budget_target=8192//5=1638 => pow2 [1,1024]; reg_bpe=20 => reg_cap=3276, budget still wins. The kernel keeps 4 fp32 inputs + t0..t4 (~9 live fp32 tiles) resident over 1024 elems ~= 36KB, but the reg model only sees 5 memory ops (20 bytes/elem). With the default 4 warps this spills registers, whereas the default [32,32] tile fits comfortably. Expect seed >10% slower than default.
code:
@helion.kernel()
def int8_bitwise_heavy(a, b, c, d):
    out = torch.empty_like(a)
    for tm, tn in hl.tile(a.size()):
        av = a[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        bv = b[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        cv = c[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        dv = d[tm, tn].to(torch.float32)
        t0 = av * bv + cv
        t1 = (av - dv) * (bv + cv)
        t2 = t0 * t0 - t1 * dv
        t3 = (t1 + t2) * (av - cv)
        t4 = t2 * bv - t3 * av + t0 * dv
        r = (t0 + t1 + t2 + t3 + t4) * 0.03125
        out[tm, tn] = r.to(out.dtype)
    return out

def make_inputs(shape):
    M, N = shape
    g = lambda: torch.randint(-8, 8, (M, N), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int8)
    return (g(), g(), g(), g())

name: bool_where_fp32
targeted_gap: bool mask (itemsize 1) + int8 operands make bytes_per_elem tiny so the byte model picks a wide tile, but a two-armed fp32 where() keeps both branch results live, doubling the true register footprint the reg model ignores
hypothesis: bpe=4 (bool load + 2 int8 loads + int8 store) => budget_target=2048; reg_bpe=16 => reg_cap=4096, budget wins => seed [1,2048]. torch.where over two fp32 arms materializes both (av*2+1) and (bv*3-1) plus the fp32 inputs live simultaneously over 2048 elems, a resident set the reg model (4 memory ops) undercounts ~2x, so at the default 4 warps the wide tile spills vs the default [32,32]. Expect seed >10% slower.
